newsitem.title: USA: U.S. markets face earnings, data minefields.
newsitem.headline: U.S. markets face earnings, data minefields.

text.p: U.S. financial markets, stung by sharp losses in stock and bonds last week, face a minefield of corporate earnings reports and economic data in the week ahead that will heighten anxiety on both on Wall Street and could rattle foreign markets.

Market analysts said that with the Dow industrials nearly 10 percent off their record highs, options expirations pending and the yield on the 30-year Treasury bond nearing the key 7.25 percent level, volatility is all but guaranteed.
"For the week ahead, I think there's going to be continued fear and trepidation," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.
The Dow Jones industrial average fell 148 points, or 2.3 percent, to 6,392 on Friday, dropping the blue chip index to its lowest closing level since Dec. 18.
The Dow's loss of 134 points last week marked the first time since 1991 that the blue chip gauge has fallen for five straight weeks.
With the decline, the Dow has tumbled 9.8 percent off its record closing high set on March 11 at 7,085.

A 10 percent drop would be the first pullback by the Dow of that magnitude in over six years, signal of a "change in character" for the wounded bull stock market, said Bruce Bittles, market strategist at J.C. Bradford.
"It would lead me to believe we're going to have a 15 percent correction here," Bittles said.
The benchmark 30-year bond was also hit by heavy selling on Friday, driving its yield up to 7.17 percent, its highest since 7.18 percent at the close on July 18.
The force behind Friday's drop in bonds and stocks was fear of higher inflation brought on by a surprisingly strong report on March inflation at the wholesale level.
On Tuesday, the government will report on March retail inflation. Economists polled by Reuters expect, on average, the Consumer Price Index to rise 0.2 percent after a 0.3 percent rise in February.

Economic data thus far have shown the U.S. economy to be robust, though with subdued inflation. But a stronger-than-expected CPI number on the back of Friday's Producer Price Index shock would be a major confirmation of the market's inflation fears.

"If you saw some signs of acceleration in the CPI, that would be real difficult for the bond market to accept," said Dana Johnson, managing director of research at First Chicago Capital Markets Inc. "I think it would have a pretty devastating impact."

Analysts said an inflation surprise would further convince market players that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates at its May 20 policy-making meeting, perhaps by as much as a half percentage point, adding to the March 25 quarter-point hike.

While interest rate concerns will weigh heavily on investors, they also must face first-quarter earnings reports from such market heavyweights as Intel Corp. and Microsoft Corp., General Motors Corp. and Merck and Co. Inc.

Analysts said that with most earnings shortfalls already pre-announced, they expect few negative surprises in the first-quarter profit numbers. Stronger-than-expected earnings from market leaders will help sooth investor sentiment.

But beyond the results from the first quarter, market players said they will be looking for indications from companies that the strong U.S. dollar is eroding their foreign sales, a sign that profits in upcoming quarters will not meet expectations.
The recent slide in U.S. stocks and bonds has done much less damage to the dollar than in the past, analysts noted.

"The feeling is the market is still set up to be buying dollars on the dips," said John Rothfield, international economist at NationsBanc CRT. "I'm looking for this to be a week of consolidation, maybe a little bit of a setback, for the dollar but with the uptrend still firmly intact."
Among other data, currency traders will focus on Thursday's report on the U.S. international trade deficit.
Added to the mix will be Friday's "double-witching" expirations of individual and index options, which often brings sharp price swings in the stock market.
